Class CpuResidencySample

java.lang.Object
oshi.hardware.common.platform.mac.CpuResidencySample
@Immutable public final class CpuResidencySample extends Object
One interval of Apple Silicon CPU performance state residency, holding the two views IOReport publishes of the same interval.

A core and the cluster it belongs to report their states separately, and the two do not always agree: a core reports the state it asked for, which is the fastest one whenever it has work, while its cluster reports the state the hardware actually ran at, which is lower whenever a power or thermal limit caps it. Measured on an M3 Pro, six busy cores each report the top state throughout while their cluster reports 3576 MHz, the figure powermetrics gives for the same interval. Both views are therefore needed: the cluster's for how fast a core ran, the core's own for whether it ran at all.

    • CpuResidencySample

      public CpuResidencySample(Map<String, Map<String,Long>> coreStates, Map<String, Map<String,Long>> complexStates)
      Creates a new sample. Both maps and the maps they contain must preserve the order in which the channel reports its states, so both are copied into insertion-ordered maps.
      Parameters:
      coreStates - the ticks each core spent in each of its states, keyed by the channel naming the core
      complexStates - the ticks each CPU complex spent in each of its states, keyed by the channel naming the complex

  • Method Details

    • getCoreStates

      public Map<String, Map<String,Long>> getCoreStates()
      Gets the residency of the individual cores, from the CPU Core Performance States channels.

      The states of one core are its idle state or states followed by one state per frequency the core's cluster can run at, in ascending frequency order.

      Returns:
      a map from the channel name identifying the core to a map from state name to ticks, in channel state order. Empty if the sample held no such channel.

    • getComplexStates

      public Map<String, Map<String,Long>> getComplexStates()
      Gets the residency of the CPU complexes, from the CPU Complex Performance States channels.

      The states are ordered as the per-core ones are, and the channels naming a complex whose residency is the state the hardware ran at can be told from the rest by their name; see CpuFrequencyResidency.realizedComplexStates(Map).

      Returns:
      a map from the channel name identifying the complex to a map from state name to ticks, in channel state order. Empty if the sample held no such channel.
